title: Process of creating Fusiomon launch post. With AI. Or as some like to call it: the 'one-click' solution.
author: MatthiasTh

comments.author: q-ue
comments.body: This doesn't give much information about what fusionmon is, or what the process actually is. Or why we should care

replies.author: MatthiasTh
replies.body: Then don't care and enjoy your day... 🙋🏻‍♂️

comments.author: icekiller333
comments.body: Why is this the 'one-click' solution when you talk about endless regenerations and prompting and finetuning?

replies.author: MatthiasTh
replies.body: Some “other” people say AI is the “one-click” solution. I would like to point this out: AI is a tool and just because you use it doesn't mean you're lazy or incompetent, but just like any designer, you have to go through several (hours or days) of work to achieve the desired result.

comments.author: MatthiasTh
comments.body:
Since the post seems to be misunderstood:  
I’ve been working on [Fusiomon](https://www.fusiomon.com/), my passion project, for over three years now - pouring thousands of hours and a lot of money into it. Fusiomon is an innovative AI-powered trading card game with a real-time in-game fusion mechanic that wouldn’t even be possible without AI.

And yet, *because* it uses AI, my work constantly gets dismissed as cheap “one-click” AI slop.

This infographic is meant to show critics and AI haters alike:  
AI is **not** a one-click solution. It’s a tool - just like any other - used to bring creative ideas to life.

replies.author: MatthiasTh
replies.body: A nice comment amongst all the fuss! Thank you so much and all the best to you too!
